title: Affine-to-global lifting for universal first order thickenings
statement: For h : Z ⟶ X and i : Z ⟶ Z', h' : Z' ⟶ X, if i is a first order thickening, i ≫ h' = h, and the universal lifting property holds whenever both test schemes are affine, then IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening h i h'.

proof.text: For a canonical pullback of a first order thickening along an open immersion, closed immersion stability supplies closedness. Mathlib Scheme.ker_ideal_of_isPullback_of_isOpenImmersion identifies the ideal on every affine open with a comap. Ideal.le_comap_pow and injectivity of the section isomorphism transport square zero. This is the proved private helper firstOrderThickening_pullback_open.

Cover an arbitrary thickened test target by its Mathlib Scheme.affineCover. Each pulled-back source is affine because its immersion is closed and hence affine (isAffine_of_isAffineHom). Apply the affine-test uniqueness to the two restricted lifts and conclude equality by Scheme.Cover.hom_ext. This proves unique_lifts_of_affine_tests without any affineness assumption on the global test.

Choose the unique local lifts on the affine cover. On a pairwise overlap, pull back the original thickening and compare the restrictions using the just-proved uniqueness for arbitrary test targets; the overlap need not be affine. Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms glues these compatible lifts. Check the base triangle on the original cover and the closed-subscheme triangle on its pullback cover, using hom_ext and the glue restriction equation. Global uniqueness follows from the preceding step. Pair the resulting lifting property with the given first order thickening and base compatibility.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04F3, paragraph beginning Before we glue affine pieces; formalized by adapting the already proved private gluing helpers in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.UniversalThickeningAffineCase to tests with both schemes affine.

lean.statement: theorem isUniversalFirstOrderThickening_of_affine_local {Z X Z' : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ X) (i : Z ⟶ Z') (h' : Z' ⟶ X) (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i) (hcomp : i ≫ h' = h) (haffine : ∀ {T T' : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] [IsAffine T'] (j : T ⟶ T') (b : T' ⟶ X) (a : T ⟶ Z), IsFirstOrderThickening j → j ≫ b = a ≫ h → ∃! a' : T' ⟶ Z', a' ≫ h' = b ∧ j ≫ a' = a ≫ i) : IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening h i h'
